Earlier this year, Apple closed part of the Apple Park Visitor Center, citing plans to "improve our store."

That space has now reopened, and the biggest change is that Apple has removed an augmented reality experience that visitors could use to view Apple Park with a special iPad.

When the Apple Park Visitor Center opened to the public in 2017, Apple promoted the AR experience as follows:

Using augmented reality technology, a three-dimensional model of the campus comes to life before your eyes. Guests are invited to explore Apple Park through an immersive, interactive experience. Visitors can learn about the world's largest naturally ventilated building and see one of the world's largest on-site solar installations. Visitors may also choose to lift the entire roof to peek into the collaborative workspaces inside.

Before this change, the Apple Park Visitor Center was divided into three zones: the AR exhibit, a traditional-style Apple Store, and a café.

Now Apple has retired the AR exhibit and expanded that space into an extension of the traditional Apple Store. According to MacRumors, this includes "Avenues" accessory display walls along the walls, as well as redesigned display tables showcasing Apple products.

The rest of the Apple Park Visitor Center, including the café, remains unchanged.

9to5Mac's take

The AR experience at the Apple Park Visitor Center was indeed unique, but nine years on, I'm starting to feel that the space could be put to better use for other purposes.

I had originally hoped Apple would try something other than turning it into a traditional retail store, but at least the café is still there, serving as a distinctive element of the Apple Park Visitor Center.
